purpose: Express/JS sibling of fastapi-saas, built for H4 (Phase H Tier 1). Measures whether IDOR's lane facts (callerAuth/operationClass) behave on a MIDDLEWARE framework the way they do on FastAPI's in-signature DI, and whether auth-bypass / admin-check / idor cross-fire on the same JS routes. Each route module has exactly ONE idor source/sink pair so the one-finding-per-file ceiling (G3) cannot confound the cross-fire reading. Scanned .js files carry NO security-tell comments; ground truth lives only here.
key_difference_from_fastapi: FastAPI expresses auth in the handler SIGNATURE (Depends/CurrentUser), so 'no auth dependency present' is a knowable fact from the route file alone -> callerAuth='unauthenticated' -> idor defers to the auth-bypass lane. Express expresses auth via MIDDLEWARE that often lives in another file or a router.use() elsewhere, so 'no visible auth' proves nothing -> the lane rule requires callerAuth='unclear' -> idor does NOT defer. The hypothesis under test (H4): this makes idor CROSS-FIRE with auth-bypass on the unauthenticated route, where FastAPI's clarity let it defer.

expected_lane_behavior.why: Authenticated (router.use(requireAuth) visible in-file), Document.findOne keyed on req.params.id with no ownerId filter and no post-fetch check. Genuine object-ownership IDOR. callerAuth=authenticated, operationClass=user_resource -> idor FIRES, no deferral. auth-bypass and admin-check should stay silent.

Privileged op (sets role; role=='admin' escalates isSuperuser), gated only by requireAuth (authenticated, NOT admin) while sibling /stats is requireAdmin-gated. admin-check FIRES (looks-guarded-but-isn't). idor's prefilter fires on req.params.id->findOne, but operationClass=administrative -> idor DEFERS to admin-check lane. auth-bypass silent (auth present).

Destructive op (removes a Document by request id) with NO auth middleware on the route, while sibling GET / passes requireAuth. auth-bypass FIRES (missing-middleware). idor's prefilter fires on req.params.id->findOne with no ownership filter; callerAuth SHOULD be 'unclear' on Express (middleware could be mounted elsewhere) -> idor does NOT defer -> idor is EXPECTED to also fire = cross-fire. On FastAPI the equivalent (users.py DELETE) deferred because in-signature DI made it provably unauthenticated. THIS ROUTE IS THE MEASUREMENT.

measured_result_2026_06_13.real_cross_fire_found: auth-bypass <-> admin-check on admin.js (both 5/5). On the auth-only-on-admin-op route, auth-bypass cross-fires into admin-check's lane (the dominant defect is the missing ADMIN gate). These two detectors have NO lane facts / routing today. This is the Express cross-fire H7 should address — NOT idor, and via the auth-bypass/admin-check pair.
